title: Introduction — The 'Eyes' Construction Revisited
description: A fully responsive, touch-enabled interactive tool that lets students construct the 'Eyes' figure step by step. Students examine a supporting line XY, set a compass radius via slider, watch realistic compass-drawing animations with visible pivot points and radius arms, find intersection points A and B, and draw the upper and lower arcs to form a symmetrical eye shape. On the final step, dragging the centre points along the perpendicular bisector changes the eye shape in real time. Works on mobile, tablet, and desktop with adaptive layout, touch drag, and fluid typography.
teaching_notes: This tool connects the Eyes construction from Grade 6 to the new concept of perpendicular bisector. The final step where students drag centres along the bisector previews the equidistant point property covered in M1.S3.T3. Emphasise that compass radius must exceed half of XY for arcs to intersect. In practice mode, students should try different radii and segment lengths. The slow 7-second animation with visible compass pivot labels ('Compass at X', 'Compass at Y', 'Centre = A', 'Centre = B') and radius arms helps students follow each construction step clearly. Touch support enables use on school tablets and phones.
instructions_for_student: Build a symmetrical eye shape step by step. Start by examining the supporting line XY, then watch how equal-radius arcs from X and Y find the centres A and B. Notice the pulsing ring showing where the compass is placed and the dashed line showing the radius arm. Finally, drag the centres along the perpendicular bisector to explore how different eye shapes emerge while symmetry is always maintained.

svgCanvas.note: All coordinates are in SVG viewBox units. The SVG scales responsively via viewBox + 100% width container.

tool_objectives.instructions_for_student: Examine the line segment XY. Use the slider to choose a compass radius. Watch the animated preview arc from X. The radius must be more than half the length of XY — why is this minimum necessary for the arcs to intersect?

Watch carefully! The compass is placed at X (see the pulsing ring and label). It sweeps an arc above. Then it lifts and is placed at Y. Where the two arcs cross is point A. Notice XA = YA — point A is equidistant from both endpoints.
Now the compass repeats below the line. Arc from X, then arc from Y — same radius. They meet at point B. Both A and B are equidistant from X and Y!

The compass is placed at A as centre and draws the upper eye arc. Then placed at B for the lower arc. The line AB is the perpendicular bisector — it passes through midpoint O at exactly 90°. This is why the eye is symmetrical!

Drag points A and B along the perpendicular bisector. Notice how different positions create different eye shapes, but symmetry is always maintained — because every point on the bisector is equidistant from X and Y!
